subject: Deployment mode options & next steps Deployment mode options & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lumina.ai>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@lumina.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode options & next steps - Lumina Labs migration

Hi Samira / Miguel,

Thanks again for the call today - good to meet the Lumina team. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we can size the best deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary goal: migrate current LLM usage with minimal regression in latency and quality, and meet EU data residency requirements.
- Current traffic: ~10k requests/day with daily peaks during business hours.
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for inference.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; potential PHI in a subset of requests (need to confirm).

Initial recommendation (high-level):
- Short term: Hosted API for quick onboarding and testing (fastest time-to-value).
- Mid-term: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and isolation during migration.
- Long-term / required if PHI & strict residency: Private VPC or on-prem deployment (we support EU-region private control plane and on-prem packages).

Questions to help us finalize recommendation and cost estimates:
1) Can you confirm whether PHI is present in any of the request payloads?
2) Are you able to share more granular qps/seq length distribution (peak qps, avg tokens per request)?
3) Do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest?

Next steps:
- I attached our Redwood_Deployment_Overview.pdf and a migration-checklist.xlsx to give you the migration sequencing and artifacts we typically need.
- If you're open, let's schedule a technical deep-dive next week with Dylan (cc'd) to map the network and compliance items.
- I'll follow up with a cost/option summary (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) once we have answers to the questions above.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: Redwood_Deployment_Overview.pdf (overview)
Attachment: migration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet of migration tasks)

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lumina.ai>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode options & next steps - Lumina Labs migration

On Sun, 30 Aug 2026 at 10:05 AM, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call today - good to meet the Lumina team. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we can size the best deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).
> 
> Summary of what I heard:
> - Primary goal: migrate current LLM usage with minimal regression in latency and quality, and meet EU data residency requirements.

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We currently use OpenAI's hosted API for generation and embeddings.
- Daily volume is ~10k requests/day; peak qps seen in EU hours is ~18-22 qps.
- Median tokens/request ~120; peak sequences can reach ~800 tokens for longer reports.
- We do have PHI in a subset (~5%) of requests - those must remain within EU jurisdiction and have customer-managed keys.

Primary ask: please send pricing and a high-level runbook for both Dedicated capacity (hosted by Redwood in EU) and Private VPC/on-prem options. For Private VPC we need to know network peering requirements, whether you support Bring-Your-Own-KMS, and typical deployment timelines.

I attached a small CSV (Lumina_current_usage.csv) with hourly qps for the last two weeks - hope that helps. We're happy to schedule the deep-dive; Miguel (cc'd) will coordinate schedules.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of AI Platform | Lumina Labs
samira.khan@lumina.ai

Attachment: Lumina_current_usage.csv (hourly qps)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lumina.ai>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@lumina.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode options & next steps - Lumina Labs migration

Thanks Samira - this is very helpful.

Short answers up front:
- BYO-KMS: yes, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private and Dedicated deployments.
- Network: Private VPC requires peering or a VPN tunnel; we'll share exact CIDR and peering docs in the tech-dive.
- Timeline: Dedicated EU deployment can be provisioned in ~2-3 weeks after contract and network setup; Private VPC or on-prem generally 6-10 weeks depending on approvals and infra procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive: 60 minutes with Dylan to go over the CSV and confirm peak shaping, sequence lengths, and network architecture (please propose 2 slots next week).
2) Commercial: I'll produce a short pricing matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and attach a draft SLA for Lumina (attached: SLA_Draft_Lumina.pdf).
3) Migration path: we usually recommend starting on Hosted API or a small Dedicated pool for canary testing, then cutover traffic when performance and compliance checks pass. The migration-checklist I attached earlier contains the step-by-step.

I've attached SLA_Draft_Lumina.pdf for your review - highlights include availability targets for Dedicated and Private, data residency commitments, and incident response timelines.

Dylan - can you add a short pre-read on network/KMS requirements? I'll propose hubspot deal updates after the tech call.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: SLA_Draft_Lumina.pdf (draft SLA)
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@lumina.ai>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@lumina.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode options & next steps - Lumina Labs migration

Marissa / Samira - quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

High-level mapping (based on the CSV & notes):
- Peak qps ~22 (EU window). Recommend Dedicated pool sized for sustained 25 qps with burst headroom to 40 qps.
- Token distribution: median ~120, 95p ~720 - plan memory/KV cache accordingly.
- Latency targets: p95 < 250ms - achievable with Dedicated using our optimized kernels and continuous batching.

Private VPC requirements (summary):
- Network: IPsec VPN or AWS VPC peering (we provide configuration snippets).
- KMS: BYO-KMS supported via Customer-managed keys; HSM options for on-prem.
- Audit & logs: We can stream audit logs to your S3/GCS or provide a secure log push to your SIEM.
- Compliance: We'll provide required artifacts (SOC 2 report, penetration test summaries) as part of the security questionnaire.

Estimated rollout timeline (rough):
- Dedicated EU: Provisioning + smoke tests = 2-3 weeks.
- Private VPC (EU): Network & infra setup + validation = 6-8 weeks.
- On-prem full: 8-12 weeks (depends on hardware lead times).

Ballpark infra sizing (example):
- Dedicated: 2x A100-equivalent nodes for the 25 qps baseline (depends on model choice & quantization).
- Private VPC: similar node counts but isolated to your VPC; we'll provide exact mapping after model selection.

I'll prepare a short slide for the deep-dive showing network diagrams and the migration cutover plan.

-Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
